result.topic_en: Riemann reduces the transformation of the heat-conduction equation to the transformation of the quadratic differential form $\sum \alpha_{\iota,\iota'} dx_\iota dx_{\iota'}$, plans how to solve the general problem, and in section 4 writes the differential equation in the case where u does not depend on one variable.

(3) $\begin{pmatrix}\alpha_{1,1}, \alpha_{2,2}, \alpha_{3,3}\\ \alpha_{2,3}, \alpha_{3,1}, \alpha_{1,2}\end{pmatrix}$ (4) $\begin{pmatrix}\beta_{1,1}, \beta_{2,2}, \beta_{3,3}\\ \beta_{2,3}, \beta_{3,1}, \beta_{1,2}\end{pmatrix}$
invenitur
$A = B\,\Sigma \pm \frac{\partial s_1}{\partial x_1}\frac{\partial s_2}{\partial x_2}\frac{\partial s_3}{\partial x_3}$
et
$\beta_{\mu,\nu} = \sum_{\iota,\iota'} \alpha_{\iota,\iota'} \frac{\partial x_\iota}{\partial s_\mu}\frac{\partial x_{\iota'}}{\partial s_\nu}$
ideoque
$\sum_{\iota,\iota'} \alpha_{\iota,\iota'} dx_\iota dx_{\iota'} = \sum_{\iota,\iota'} \beta_{\iota,\iota'} ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}$
et
$\frac{h}{A} = \frac{k}{B}$
Unde facile perspicitur transformationem
aequationis (I) reduci posse ad transformationem
expressionis $\sum_{\iota,\iota'} \alpha_{\iota,\iota'} dx_\iota dx_{\iota'}$.
Quae quum ita sint, problema nostrum generale
hoc modo solvere possumus, ut primum quaeramus,
quales esse debeant functiones $b_{\iota,\iota'}$ et $k$ ipsarum $s_1, s_2, s_3$,
ut u ab una harum quantitatum non pendere
possit. Qua quaestione soluta expressio $\Sigma \beta_{\iota,\iota'} ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}$
formari [-possit-] poterit. Tum ut, datis valoribus
quantitatum $a_{\iota,\iota'}$ et quantitatis $h$, inveniamus, num
u functio temporis et duarum tantum variabilium
fieri [-pos-] possit et quibusnam in casibus, quaerendum
est, an expressio illa $\Sigma \beta_{\iota,\iota'} ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}$ in formam datam
transformari possit; et hanc quaestionem infra
videbimus eadem fere methodo tractari posse, qua
Gauss in theoria superficierum curvarum usus est.

Primum igitur quaeramus, quales esse debeant
functiones $b_{\iota,\iota'}$ et $k$ ipsarum $s_1, s_2, s_3$, ut u ab una
harum quantitatum non pendere possit. Ut deno-
tationem simpliciorem reddamus, quantitates $s_1, s_2, s_3$
per $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ designemus et formam (2) per
$\begin{pmatrix}a, b, c\\ a', b', c'\end{pmatrix}$
si u a [-a-] $\gamma$ non pendet, aequatio differentialis
erit formae
(II) $a\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\alpha^2} + 2c'\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta} + b\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\beta^2} + e\frac{\partial u}{\partial\alpha} + f\frac{\partial u}{\partial\beta} - k\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = F = 0$
posito
$\frac{\partial a}{\partial\alpha} + \frac{\partial c'}{\partial\beta} + \frac{\partial b'}{\partial\gamma} = e \quad \frac{\partial b}{\partial\beta} + \frac{\partial c'}{\partial\alpha} + \frac{\partial a'}{\partial\gamma} = f.$

items.english: We can solve our general problem in this way: first we investigate what the functions b and k of s1, s2, s3 must be so that u can be independent of one of these quantities.

items.english: To find whether u can become a function of time and only two variables, and in which cases, one must investigate whether that expression can be transformed into the given form.

items.english: And we shall see below that this question can be treated by almost the same method that Gauss used in the theory of curved surfaces.
